name: Drag and drop
first: Moving a value from one view, or from one app, to another, by dragging it and dropping it, with the value carried as data of a transferable type.

dependsOn.why: A drag carries a value of a transferable type, as data, and the drop turns the data back into values.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The constant `city` is a string, which is transferable, as `Trip` is on the page of Transferable.

dependsOn.why: A drag starts with a touch that the view recognizes, which the drag modifier adds for it.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The modifier `draggable(city)` adds to the `Text` the gestures for dragging it, as `gesture(drag)` adds a drag on the page of Gesture.

what.is: Drag and drop moves a value from one view to another, or from one app to another. The modifier `draggable` makes a view the start of a drag, carrying a value of a transferable type. The modifier `dropDestination` makes a view a place to drop values of one type, and calls its closure with the values that were dropped.
what.afterExample: The card Lima can be dragged, and the gray area takes strings that are dropped on it. A drag carries the string as data: line 11 turns it into plain text, as the drag would, and line 12 prints that data as text: {{Lima}}. A program with no window has no finger to drag, so the closure of the drop never runs.
what.problem: Users expect to move things by dragging them, such as a photo into a trip, or a trip into another app. Both sides must agree on what the data is. Drag and drop carries the value as data of a transferable type, so any side that reads that kind of data can take it.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that `draggable` adds the gestures for drag and drop to the view, and makes a picture of the view to show under the finger. When the user drops on a view with `dropDestination`, the data is turned back into values of the type it names, here `String`, and its closure gets them, with the point of the drop. The closure returns true when it took the values.

when.text: Use it for moving items where people expect it, such as sorting trips, or adding a photo from another app.
Don't make dragging the only way to do something. Some users cannot drag, so give a button or a menu as well.
